done_when: Forge's shipped review instructions say a crash or interrupt window under a second, or a case a simple fail-closed rule in the change already covers, is at most P2 unless it loses data or weakens security, and a request for more test variations is P2 unless it names a scenario the current tests pass while the code is broken; the cold-read instructions say to prefer one blunt fail-closed rule with one test over listing every case, and not to raise crash windows under a second; the worker brief says one command-level test per rule; Forge's own AGENTS.md keeps only its Forge-specific review rules (new and existing client repos, guide updates). New and existing repos: every repo gets the rules through the templates on its next forge sync after upgrading; nothing in forge.toml changes. One test checks the synced review, cold-read and brief text carry the rules.
why: The rules that stop reviews and plan reads from over-reaching (blunt fail-closed rules over crash windows, one test per rule) live only in Forge's own AGENTS.md, so client repos' reviews and plan reads keep chasing edge cases and extra tests
